insights.summary: FY26 revenue roughly doubled to ₹112 Cr with PAT of ₹17 Cr, driven by government car-parking projects in the North-East (Shillong Smart City) and elevators, but operating cash flow was –₹17 Cr as government payments slowed. Management targets ~80%+ growth in FY27 as L.T. now executes Ricardo's home-lift orders (₹70-80 Cr order book, merger filing end-May) on top of a ₹250 Cr order book, with EBITDA margin similar to FY26's ~24%, and is building a new plant (~₹25 Cr) for ₹350-400 Cr of revenue by March 2027. It is also in talks to buy an international car-parking technology company.

what_changed.text: B2C share target for FY27 set at ~35% (Jan call talked of 50-60% by FY28)
New plant for ₹350-400 Cr revenue by Q4 FY27
Exports started: Malaysia and Australia under the Ricardo brand at ~50% higher prices

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: We feel that now we are just at the starting line and the best is going to come in the years ahead.

analyst_questions.topic: Capacity bottleneck before the new plant
analyst_questions.answer: Outsourcing some processes, extra machines and a rented shed; must exceed the ₹150-160 Cr capacity.

analyst_questions.topic: Goodwill impairment ₹7 Cr and 17x jump in other current assets

analyst_questions.answer: Bills take 3-4 months to clear; March payments slipped into April.
Prices raised from April; escalation clauses on government contracts.

red_flags.text: Could not explain a ₹7 Cr goodwill impairment or a 17x rise in other current assets; CFO absent.
Results were re-uploaded because of errors.
Operating cash flow negative for three years; slow government payments.
Ricardo orders executed before the merger is approved ('at arm's length').
